tables-quiz-choice.title: Choose table markup for structured data
tables-quiz-choice.prompt: Which element represents one row in an HTML table?
tables-quiz-choice.hint: Think row, not cell or section.

help.concept: The tr element groups the cells that make up one table row.
help.hint_1: A td is one data cell.
help.hint_2: Choose the element whose name means table row.

tables-quiz-multi.title: Recognize table structure
tables-quiz-multi.hint: Choose elements whose purposes are part of table structure.

help.concept: th labels header cells and tbody groups body rows.
help.hint_1: One correct answer is a cell type; the other is a row group.
help.hint_2: Ignore elements from other HTML concepts.

tables-quiz-order.title: Order a simple table
tables-quiz-order.prompt: Arrange the tokens into a table containing one data row.
tables-quiz-order.hint: The table container surrounds its row.

help.hint_2: Place the row before closing table.

tables-quiz-blank.title: Choose the correct header cell
tables-quiz-blank.prompt: Fill the blank with the element that marks Time as a table header cell.
tables-quiz-blank.hint: The missing cell labels a column.

help.concept: Header cells use th rather than td.
help.hint_1: The neighboring Session cell is also a header.
help.hint_2: Choose the complete th element for Time.

table-data.title: Use a table for row-and-column relationships
table-data.bodyMarkdown:
Tables are for data where values relate across rows and columns. Use `<table>` for the structure, `<tr>` for each row, `<th>` for header cells, and `<td>` for data cells.

A list is better for a simple collection; a table is better when each row shares the same fields.

thead-tbody.title: Separate headers from data with thead and tbody
thead-tbody.bodyMarkdown:
`<thead>` groups header rows and `<tbody>` groups the main data rows. This makes a larger table easier to understand.

Use one `<tr>` per row and keep the same logical columns from row to row.
